rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a multimodal (RNA + image) configuration with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, which are promising but underexplored. It clarifies the effectiveness of combining strong encoders (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l) with complex interaction modeling. This balances exploration of key design choices (multimodal, transformer) while using moderate cost compared to more expensive configurations.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, ViT, transformer, weighted) achieves 58.56% accuracy. This experiment tests replacing ViT with resnet50 (simpler image encoder) and avgpool (cheaper aggregation) while keeping weighted fusion. It clarifies if simpler components can maintain accuracy while reducing cost. This balances exploration (testing alternatives to ViT/transformer) and exploitation (building on multiprofile/multimodal success). Expected cost is lower than config_001 (4.55 GPU hours) due to resnet50 and avgpool, making it a cost-effective next step.

The existing evidence shows config_007 (avgpool + weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.639) but uses resnet50. Testing config_008 (transformer + weighted fusion) with the same RNA encoder and image encoder will clarify if transformer aggregation improves accuracy further. This balances exploration of a potentially more powerful aggregation method against the cost (estimated ~15 GPU hours), which is justified given the strong prior performance of similar configurations.

Existing evidence shows config_007 (resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l while keeping other components identical to config_007, clarifying if the image encoder choice significantly impacts performance. It balances exploration (testing a larger, more complex image encoder) with exploitation (maintaining proven components). Expected cost is slightly higher than config_007 (~10.60 GPU hours), but the potential to improve accuracy justifies the cost given the budget constraint.

The existing evidence shows config_007 (accuracy 0.639) is the best so far but has high cost (10.6 GPU hours). This experiment tests using scgpt RNA encoder (potentially more expressive) with resnet50 image encoder (already shown effective) and weighted fusion (proven to work well), but with transformer aggregation (which may improve performance). It balances exploration (testing a new RNA encoder) and exploitation (using proven image encoder and fusion). Expected cost is ~12 GPU hours, which is reasonable given the potential for higher accuracy compared to cheaper alternatives with similar components.

Existing evidence shows config_007 (resnet50, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves 0.6390 accuracy. This experiment tests changing fusion to concat while keeping resnet50 and avgpool, which could clarify if fusion method impacts performance. It's a low-cost variation of a top-performing configuration, balancing exploration of key design choices with exploitation of proven components.

The existing evidence shows config_007 (0.639 accuracy) and config_026 (0.635 accuracy) are top performers with multimodal settings. This experiment tests using transformer aggregation (which outperformed avgpool in config_001/config_008) with scvi_n200 RNA encoder (more expressive than pca_n2000) while retaining resnet50 image encoder (proven effective in config_007). It clarifies if combining transformer aggregation with a more sophisticated RNA encoder can surpass current bests. Expected cost ~12 GPU hours (moderate for complex architecture), balancing exploration of aggregation methods with proven image encoder.

Existing evidence shows config_019 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with concat fusion instead of weighted fusion, clarifying whether fusion method impacts performance. The expected cost (similar to config_019's 6.22 GPU hours) is reasonable, allowing a final experiment to explore other promising directions if needed.

Existing evidence shows that config_019 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests a logical extension by using a larger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, which could improve accuracy while maintaining similar cost. It clarifies whether the choice of image encoder or fusion method impacts performance, balancing exploitation of scvi_n200's strength with exploration of larger models. Expected cost is similar to config_019 (6.22 GPU hours).

The existing evidence shows config_036 (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.7207) so far. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion type from concat to weighted (while keeping scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, and transformer aggregation) could improve accuracy. It clarifies the impact of fusion type on performance, with a low expected cost (4.65 GPU hours) similar to config_036. This balances exploitation of the current best configuration and exploration of a critical design choice.
